t: You're outside the building on Gordon Square in Bloomsbury that housed Dr Williams's Library, also known as University Hall. The library was a small research library, founded in 1729, focused on Nonconformist theology and history. It occupied this building from 1890 until 2025. It takes its name from Daniel Williams, a Welsh theologian and minister in the Presbyterian tradition, meaning a Christian outside the Church of England. His legacy led to the library's creation, and it became a centre for research on English Dissenters.
